line:
"Brann, keep working that brass ring with whatever oil you have, I'll come back for it." I leave the reliquary seated in the socket, drop down the trapdoor, and take the third step above the doorway just as the crate gives.

As the first pikemen crowd Kit's shield, I cast Faerie Fire at the doorway and the shingle beyond, outlining all of them in light so Kit's attacks have advantage, and call, "Hit the lit ones, Kit, and tell me when you need Healing Word."

input.add_to_description: Day 10 ~7:30 AM: fight at the north door. Kit holds the doorway; Wren on the stair cast Faerie Fire over the pikemen and Sparrow (Pikeman 1 saved); the Grey Cloak stayed back on the shingle, outside the light. Kit hit Pikeman 2.

entries.text: notebook: updated The Gullspit Light

You drop down the trapdoor and take the third step above the doorway just as the crate gives. The door bursts inward in a spray of splinters, and the pikes come through on the heels of it. Kit takes them on her shield and the doorframe, and holds, but they are quick. One spear thrust gets under her guard for five, another for four, and the crossbow bolt Sparrow sends past the pikemen's shoulders whines off the stone. Kit is at 11 of her 20 hit points. She hasn't made a sound.

Your turn comes. You throw out a hand and sing a bright, mocking note, and Faerie Fire blooms over the doorway and the shingle beyond. Two of the three pikemen and Sparrow himself are outlined in violet light, their edges glowing and their shadows gone. The third pikeman twists aside in time and keeps his dark outline. The grey-cloaked figure stands further back on the stones, outside the glow and watching, with no sign of hurry. You hold the spell with your concentration, and you have one spell slot left.

Kit doesn't need to be told twice. Her longsword takes the lit pikeman on the doorstep squarely, with advantage, and bites for seven. He staggers, gasping, but he is still up, his shield dented and bleeding down the arm.

Round two is coming. Kit is at 11 hit points, Pikeman 2 is hurt and glowing, Sparrow is glowing and has a cold look on his face. The Grey Cloak still hasn't moved. It's your turn next, after theirs.

(Outside the story: the order this round is the pikemen, then Sparrow, then you, then Kit. Tell me what Wren does when it comes to you.)

sheet.name: Wren Ashgrove
sheet.opening: Wren Ashgrove, a half-elf bard of about nineteen with a quick grin and a sharper tongue, arrives at dusk in the river-market town of Marrowford, a few weeks after fleeing the caravan of her mentor Corvin Tallowmere. She was raised by him as a storyteller's apprentice, and she left in the night at a river crossing with his ledger of forged tales sold to nobles (its pages now hidden in the binding of her road-psalter), a few of his best forgeries, and a head start. She carries a brass lantern-shaped reliquary of the Lantern-Bearer, a gentle road-god of travelers and tale-tellers whom Corvin worshipped only as cover; it holds a curl of yellowed parchment in an unknown hand that may be a true blessing or another forgery. She does not know if Corvin has sent anyone after her. Her ideal: stories should be free, and truth is whatever people can be made to believe. Her bond: find the nobles Corvin cheated and decide whether to expose him or quietly fix what he did. Her flaw: she can't resist a secret, and she lies even when the truth would serve her better. She has 15 gp, a rapier, a dagger, leather armor, a lute, a diplomat's pack with blank paper and sealing wax, and was raised with no memory of her birth family. The hook: as she reaches the market square, she spots a caravan wagon with Corvin's painted shrine-lantern sigil parked at the edge of town, but no sign of Corvin. A frightened young page in a minor noble's livery is pressing a sealed letter into the hands of the wagon's driver, and the seal looks like one Wren has seen in the ledger. Something is happening that links her stolen ledger to a noble house, and it needs a quick-witted liar to either sort it out or be caught in it. Open on Wren in the square, with the choice of how to approach the wagon and the page, and a locked iron-bound strongbox on the wagon's tailboard that she itches to poke at.

To do so, you use a bonus action on your turn to choose one creature other than yourself within 60 feet of you who can hear you. That creature gains one Bardic Inspiration die, a d6. Once within the next 10 minutes, the creature can roll the die and add the number rolled to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes. Song of Rest (d6): Beginning at 2nd level, you can use soothing music or oration to help revitalize your wounded allies during a short rest. If you or any friendly creatures who can hear your performance regain hit points at the end of the short rest by spending one or more Hit Dice, each of those creatures regains an extra 1d6 hit points.  The extra hit points increase when you reach certain levels in this class: to 1d8 at 9th level, to 1d10 at 13th level, and to 1d12 at 17th level. At level 2: extra 1d6 hit points.

Shelter of the Faithful (Acolyte): As an acolyte, you command the respect of those who share your faith, and you can perform the religious ceremonies of your deity. You and your adventuring companions can expect to receive free healing and care at a temple, shrine, or other established presence of your faith, though you must provide any material components needed for spells. Those who share your religion will support you (but only you) at a modest lifestyle. You might also have ties to a specific temple dedicated to your chosen deity or pantheon, and you have a residence there. This could be the temple where you used to serve, if you remain on good terms with it, or a temple where you have found a new home. While near your temple, you can call upon the priests for assistance, provided the assistance you ask for is not hazardous and you remain in good standing with your temple.

input.add_to_description: Day 10 ~7:30 AM: fight at the north door. Three pike-hands (Guard stats) vs Kit in the doorway; Wren cast Faerie Fire (only Pike 3 failed). Kit at 11/20 after a crit; Pike 3 wounded. Sparrow and the Grey Cloak watch from the landing and have not engaged.

entries.text: notebook: updated The Gullspit Light

You drop through the trapdoor and take the third step above the door just as the crate splinters. The door bursts inward, and you fling Faerie Fire out over the doorway and the shingle beyond. It's a ragged cast. Only one pikeman, the rearmost of the three, fails his save and is outlined in blue-green light. The other two shake it off. You're concentrating on the spell now, and you have one slot left.

Kit had already set her shield and squared up in the doorway to fight defensively, and it saved her from worse. The first pikeman's thrust caught her on a lucky blow, a natural 20 despite the disadvantage, and opened her side for 9. She's at 11 of 20. The other two pikes skid off her shield and chain.

Her answer is quick and hard. Her longsword, with advantage against the lit man, takes him across the thigh for 5. He staggers but is still up. Behind the three, in the grey light on the landing, you can just make out Sparrow's brown coat and the hooded Grey Cloak, who are not coming through yet. They're watching.

It's round 2 and your turn. You hold Faerie Fire, and Kit is hurt but upright, with your Bardic Inspiration die unspent. You have one bonus action, and the stair to climb or hold. What does Wren do?

line:
"A word, Sparrow? Gladly." I keep Ember still and the staff upright, and call to the grey figure, clear enough to carry down the causeway and into the reeds. "Sir, your man says you'd like a word, so take off your hood, let's use your own name, and tell me what you want with a girl and her mother's lamp."

I let that sit a breath, then add, "Because I've been to Thornhallow's register, sir, and Aldous Verrel the younger was baptised a servant's child and buried at three, and his grave doesn't open for a man in a grey cloak." As I finish I swing the lamp-staff up and high, the signal, and cast Faerie Fire at the whole line of them on the road.

input.add_to_description: Day 15 ~2:06 PM: fight begins at the culvert. Wren challenged the Grey Cloak by name and cited the register; his men opened fire first (crossbow hit Wren for 9, Sparrow's hand crossbow for 6: Wren at 2 HP). Five pikemen (Bandit 1-5) and Sparrow vs Wren, Kit; Grey Cloak (Noble stats) stands back at ~75 ft. Wren has not yet raised the staff or cast Faerie Fire.

entries.text: notebook: updated Gannet Causeway

You call it out clear and carrying: his name, the register, the dead child's grave. For a heartbeat the grey figure doesn't move. Then a hand lifts inside the cloak, and the whole line answers before you can raise the staff.

Two crossbows crack from the line. One bolt goes wide of you. The other punches into your ribs for 9. Sparrow, closing the distance at a quick walk, fires his hand crossbow at you from forty-odd feet, and it takes you too, for 6. You are at 2 of 17 hit points and still in the saddle. Three pikemen sprint up the causeway toward Kit. Kit sets her shield and stays at the wheel beside you, covering you with her body and Dodging, so attacks against her have disadvantage. The tall man in grey hasn't moved. His ring flashes once.

It is round 1 and you act last. The pikemen are about fifteen feet from Kit. Sparrow is some forty feet off, and the other two crossbowmen and the Grey Cloak are in the line at about seventy-five. The staff is in your hand and your signal is ready for the guards. One hit will drop you. You have three 1st-level slots, three Bardic Inspirations, and Kit beside you. What does Wren do?

sheet.name: Wren Ashgrove
sheet.opening: Wren Ashgrove, a half-elf bard of about nineteen with a quick grin and a sharper tongue, arrives at dusk in the river-market town of Marrowford, a few weeks after fleeing the caravan of her mentor Corvin Tallowmere. She was raised by him as a storyteller's apprentice, and she left in the night at a river crossing with his ledger of forged tales sold to nobles (its pages now hidden in the binding of her road-psalter), a few of his best forgeries, and a head start. She carries a brass lantern-shaped reliquary of the Lantern-Bearer, a gentle road-god of travelers and tale-tellers whom Corvin worshipped only as cover; it holds a curl of yellowed parchment in an unknown hand that may be a true blessing or another forgery. She does not know if Corvin has sent anyone after her. Her ideal: stories should be free, and truth is whatever people can be made to believe. Her bond: find the nobles Corvin cheated and decide whether to expose him or quietly fix what he did. Her flaw: she can't resist a secret, and she lies even when the truth would serve her better. She has 15 gp, a rapier, a dagger, leather armor, a lute, a diplomat's pack with blank paper and sealing wax, and was raised with no memory of her birth family. The hook: as she reaches the market square, she spots a caravan wagon with Corvin's painted shrine-lantern sigil parked at the edge of town, but no sign of Corvin. A frightened young page in a minor noble's livery is pressing a sealed letter into the hands of the wagon's driver, and the seal looks like one Wren has seen in the ledger. Something is happening that links her stolen ledger to a noble house, and it needs a quick-witted liar to either sort it out or be caught in it. Open on Wren in the square, with the choice of how to approach the wagon and the page, and a locked iron-bound strongbox on the wagon's tailboard that she itches to poke at.

features: Darkvision: You have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.
Fey Ancestry: You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic cannot put you to sleep.
Skill Versatility: You gain proficiency in two skills of your choice.

Bardic Inspiration (d6): You can inspire others through stirring words or music. To do so, you use a bonus action on your turn to choose one creature other than yourself within 60 feet of you who can hear you. That creature gains one Bardic Inspiration die, a d6. Once within the next 10 minutes, the creature can roll the die and add the number rolled to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes. The creature can wait until after it rolls the d20 before deciding to use the Bardic Inspiration die, but must decide before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. Once the Bardic Inspiration die is rolled, it is lost. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once). You regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest.  Your Bardic Inspiration die changes when you reach certain levels in this class. The die becomes a d8 at 5th level, a d10 at 10th level, and a d12 at 15th level. At level 2: Bardic Inspiration die d6.
Jack of All Trades: Starting at 2nd level, you can add half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, to any ability check you make that doesn't already include your proficiency bonus.

Song of Rest (d6): Beginning at 2nd level, you can use soothing music or oration to help revitalize your wounded allies during a short rest. If you or any friendly creatures who can hear your performance regain hit points at the end of the short rest by spending one or more Hit Dice, each of those creatures regains an extra 1d6 hit points.  The extra hit points increase when you reach certain levels in this class: to 1d8 at 9th level, to 1d10 at 13th level, and to 1d12 at 17th level. At level 2: extra 1d6 hit points.

Shelter of the Faithful (Acolyte): As an acolyte, you command the respect of those who share your faith, and you can perform the religious ceremonies of your deity. You and your adventuring companions can expect to receive free healing and care at a temple, shrine, or other established presence of your faith, though you must provide any material components needed for spells. Those who share your religion will support you (but only you) at a modest lifestyle. You might also have ties to a specific temple dedicated to your chosen deity or pantheon, and you have a residence there. This could be the temple where you used to serve, if you remain on good terms with it, or a temple where you have found a new home. While near your temple, you can call upon the priests for assistance, provided the assistance you ask for is not hazardous and you remain in good standing with your temple.

line:
"A word, Sparrow? Gladly." I keep Ember still and the staff upright, and call to the grey figure, clear enough to carry down the causeway and into the reeds. "Sir, your man says you'd like a word, so take off your hood, let's use your own name, and tell me what you want with a girl and her mother's lamp."

I let that sit a breath, then add, "Because I've been to Thornhallow's register, sir, and Aldous Verrel the younger was baptised a servant's child and buried at three, and his grave doesn't open for a man in a grey cloak." As I finish I swing the lamp-staff up and high, the signal, and cast Faerie Fire at the whole line of them on the road.

input.add_to_description: Day 15 ~2:05 PM: fight begins at the culvert. Wren named the register leaf's truth aloud, raised the staff (guards' signal) and cast Faerie Fire: Pikemen 2, 4, 5 lit; Sparrow, the Grey Cloak, Pikemen 1 and 3 resisted. Grey Cloak hasn't answered or unhooded.

entries.text: notebook: updated Gannet Causeway

Your voice carries down the causeway and into the reeds. Sparrow's smile slips a notch at "buried at three." The grey figure says nothing and does not lift his hood. You thrust the lamp-staff high, and behind you the reeds erupt with Pell's cry and the clatter of guards running for both ends of the culvert.

One note on range: thirty paces is a little beyond Faerie Fire's sixty feet, so Ember steps forward twenty feet first, still level with the wagon's front wheel. Then you speak the word. Violet light bursts over the road and the pikemen. Pikemen 2, 4 and 5 are outlined, glowing, and anyone attacking them has advantage. Pikemen 1 and 3 dodge it (one with a natural 20). Sparrow dodges it too, with a 16, and so does the grey figure, with an 18. He stands untouched at the back and, for the first time, you see his hood turn toward you.

Round 1, your turn. You have used your action and some movement, and Faerie Fire needs your concentration. You still have your bonus action, two 1st-level slots and three Bardic Inspirations. Kit is at the wheel with her shield up. After you, Sparrow acts, then the Grey Cloak, then the pikemen, then Kit.

What does Wren do with her bonus action?
